decisions.decision: The vendor deviceId is NOT sensitive; it may enter accessory context and runtime logs
decisions.rationale: User call 2026-08-29, then confirmed by measurement: <account-id> is an opaque 24-char lowercase hex key, not an email. D-027 still keeps it out of public artifacts.

decisions.decision: A valid empty inventory list COUNTS toward confirmed removal
decisions.rationale: User chose this over the recommendation, and it is the more conservative call on the axis that matters — it keeps D-029 exactly as locked, where only FAILED inventories never count.

decisions.decision: Build the full capability-descriptor family registry per DEV-02
decisions.rationale: User choice over a minimal interface. Extends the DeviceFamily seam already in src/device/family.ts.

decisions.decision: Degraded accessories set StatusActive false and leave StatusFault at NO_FAULT
decisions.rationale: User asked for this decided in Phase 2 rather than deferred. StatusActive=false says the plugin cannot vouch for the value, which is true; StatusFault=GENERAL_FAULT would assert a device fault the plugin has no basis for. Verified against the pinned hap-nodejs definitions. Apple Home visibility of that state is a recorded Phase 3 concern.

context_notes:
Working tree clean, 173 commits on features/phase-02-safe-gemini-discovery-and-identity, nothing pushed, main untouched at 95f999b.

The defining event of this session: pointing the plugin at the real vendor API found that the shipped REST client could not talk to it AT ALL. GET /devices returns { devices: [...] } not a bare array, GET /devices/{id} returns { device: {...} } under a different singular key, and serialNumber lives at attributes.serialNumber. 464 unit tests and 35 Cucumber scenarios passed against that client, through code review, verification, Nyquist validation and a security audit reaching threats_open 0 — because the fixtures AND the Cucumber fake were built from the same wrong assumption as the production code. Fixed and verified 10/10 in quick task 260829-gx6.

The same lesson recurred one level up: a plan's failing-scenario grep was derived by reading the Cucumber formatter source and independently 'confirmed' by a reviewer reading the same source. Both wrong — it matched 0 of 16 real failures and would have reported a red gate as green. The executor caught it by running Cucumber.

UAT 2 and 3 now PASS with recorded evidence: heartbeat on shadow/update/accepted at exactly 898s (RES-01's two-missed-heartbeat rule now rests on a measurement), and a real SigV4 handshake with 0 errors (the fake broker accepts every signature, so the suite structurally could not test it).

pre-commit hooks were installed for the first time — .git/hooks previously held only .sample files, so every prior commit including all 153 from Phase 1 went in with no automatic enforcement. Both stages now fire; gitlint passes on all recent messages. Note this is local-only and does not survive a fresh clone.

Live API probes preserved at ~/bg-uat-probes/ with a README; credentials at ~/.gs-uat.env (gs, not bg).

Process note for the next session: an isolated executor CANNOT see untracked files from the shared checkout — worktrees share the object database and refs, not working-tree files. Commit the PLAN before dispatching, which is what the worktree-pre-dispatch-commit step exists for. Skipping it cost one halted dispatch.
